Subject: Private VPC connectivity options, egress IPs, and technical owners (post-demo)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the Private VPC track: 

Summary of options we discussed (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to prod, logs/data through Redwood host (not an option for regulated workloads like yours).
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool (good if you need predictable throughput but still want managed egress through Redwood).
- Private VPC (your preference): customer-hosted network with either PrivateLink or VPC peering to our service plane.

What we need from Clearwater to finalize the technical path:
1) Expected QPS / token throughput (ballpark) so we can size Dedicated vs Private capacity if you choose Dedicated fallback.
2) Preferred connectivity model: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) or VPC peering. We listed pros/cons in the attached one-pager.
3) Egress allowlist requirements — do you need static egress IPs from Redwood, or will you allow our PrivateLink ENIs? If peering, which NAT/egress model do you prefer?
4) KMS/Key custody constraints (bring-your-own-key needed?) and SOC2 evidence requirements for the procurement packet.

Proposed immediate owners and asks: 
- Clearwater: provide a short network inventory (subnet ranges, region, NAT/firewall owners) — NetworkOps (copied).
- Redwood: provide a connectivity playbook and example SOW (Marissa will own).
- Redwood SE: Ben will confirm exact egress IPs and certificate/cname needs for PrivateLink.

Attachments: clearwater_network_matrix.xlsx (template for subnets/contacts), redwood_privatelink-vs-peering-onepager.pdf

Can we aim to have the network inventory filled by Friday (Jun 23)? If so we'll schedule a dedicated netops session next week.

Thanks,

Grace — great recap, thanks. A couple clarifying Qs from our side before we fill the sheet: 

- Egress IPs: our security/compliance team needs a list of static IPs (CIDR / single IPv4s) that we can enter into our firewall allowlist. If PrivateLink uses ENIs in our VPC, will Redwood provide static ENI IPs or a predictable range?
- TLS / certs: For PrivateLink, do you require us to provision a CNAME for endpoint verification or will you present a Redwood-managed cert?
- Peering: if we choose VPC peering, will Redwood accept cross-account peering in our main production VPC, or do you prefer a dedicated peering VPC?

Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity options, egress IPs, and technical owners (post-demo)

Alex / Priya — Ben from Redwood SE here. Quick technical clarifications to make the allowlist/inventory work smoother: 

1) PrivateLink IPs: PrivateLink uses ENIs in your VPC and those ENIs get addresses from your subnets. We don't supply static "Redwood-run" IPs for an ENI inside your VPC; instead, when using PrivateLink you allow egress to the service via the interface endpoint. If your firewall policy requires explicit remote IPs, the peering model with NAT egress from Redwood may be easier because we can provide a fixed egress pool (list of public IPs) that traffic will originate from.

2) Peering model: with VPC peering traffic stays internal and you control route tables. Downsides: peering requires route table changes and cross-account routes; it's often simpler for banks to use PrivateLink due to tighter segmentation and no transitive routing concerns.

3) TLS / certs: Redwood will present a Redwood-managed cert for the service endpoint. For mTLS or mutual auth we can support client certs or token-based mTLS; if you need strict mutual TLS we'll need to align on cert rotation and CA trust chain (Karthik can run through options).

4) KMS: we support BYOK via an external KMS/HSM — if you require customer-managed keys for model payloads at rest we will include KMS calls in the SOW.

Actionable next steps from Redwood SE: 
- I'll prepare a short tech note comparing PrivateLink vs peering with expected firewall rule snippets and a sample public egress IP block if you go with peering.
- Marissa will draft a sample SOW and procurement timelines.
- Can we schedule 30 minutes with your NetworkOps next Tue (Jun 26) 10:00–10:30 PT? Grace / Marissa / Karthik and I will join.

Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity options, egress IPs, and technical owners (post-demo)

Thanks Ben / Grace — this is helpful. Quick notes from Network/Infosec: 

- We prefer PrivateLink for production due to tighter segmentation and auditability. Our main ask is: a short runbook showing the interface endpoint lifecycle (creation, cert renewal, how we validate service identity) and a list of permissions the endpoint owner must grant (IAM policy examples).
- If you can supply recommended security groups/rules and the minimum subnet sizes (AZ counts), that will speed our internal approvals.
- We will not accept unknown public egress IPs on the production VPC without a secondary approval; peering + Redwood NAT with a provided public egress pool is an acceptable alternative for non-prod.

We will fill the attached inventory by EOD Fri and confirm the Tue 10:00 PT slot. Also please include a procurement checklist and anticipated SOW duration (legal + security review estimates) in the SOW doc.

Priya Singh
Director, Infrastructure Security | Clearwater Bank
priya.singh@clearwaterbank.com
